title: Use the PJRT wheel built with NCCL 2.30.7 headers
body:
Bump the ARM64 GPU PJRT wheel from XLA `3a8f3392723e` to [`b040736f2c4a`](https://github.com/marin-community/xla/releases/tag/marin-xla-pjrt-20260909-b040736f2c4a), adopting the NCCL 2.30.7 build-header default from [marin-community/xla#22](https://github.com/marin-community/xla/pull/22). This aligns compiled NCCL headers with the 2.30.7 runtime in Marin's GPU training lock. JAX stays at 0.11.1, and all other data in `uv.lock` is unchanged.

The hero launcher starts `hero-ragged_a2a-nccl2307-ep-step81k` from the pooled-wave lineage's step-81716 handoff, giving the promoted wheel its own run tree. It does not restore from the trial run's tree.

The release passed ragged all-to-all correctness checks on two GB200 GPUs with NCCL runtime 2.31.2, including confirmation that XLA's ragged all-to-all device kernel executed. Marin's four-GB200 ragged-EP gate also passed with the locked NCCL 2.30.7 runtime, checking forward outputs, gradients, and dropped assignments against a dense reference across four seeds.

At hero scale on 2026-09-09 (11 racks, 704 GPUs, restoring `step-81716`), the `3a8f3392723e` wheel hung four of four attempts on one rack's expert-parallel domain (rack indices 7, 9, 1, 2 after 43, 0, 0, 0 steps), with the #8870 signature: one rack at half CPU, every cross-rack AllReduce one member exactly three operations behind. A pre-merge build of this change (`b183c591142c`, the same source) then ran 225 clean steps including a 5.4 TB checkpoint, tracking the pooled-wave control step for step at −0.0064 nats with drops 1e-4 vs 3.4e-2 and MFU 23.3% vs 21.5%. Evidence is on marin-community/marin#8506; the mechanism is the 2.29.7 compat shim's per-rack LSA cliques without bounded barriers.

`trigger_hero.sh` relaunches the hero as `hero-ragged_a2a-nccl2307-ep-step81k` from the same `step-81716` handoff, so the first 200 steps replay the validated window against the control and the lineage stays on main commits.

Part of #8870.
